short: How many months a business can operate before it runs out of cash.
seoTitle: Cash Runway — Meaning, Formula and Example
metaDescription: Cash runway is how many months a business can operate at its current burn rate before the money runs out. The formula, and why profit does not protect it.
definition: Cash runway is how long a business can keep operating at its current rate of cash burn before it runs out of money, usually expressed in months.
bodyHtml:
Why cash runway matters

It is the single most useful number a small business can carry in its head, and it is not the same as profit. A business can be profitable on paper and still have three months of runway if receivables are slow and stock is heavy.

What shortens runway

Runway shortens when days sales outstanding stretches, when stock builds up, or when payables get compressed by a statutory deadline. Track it monthly alongside the cash flow statement rather than calculating it once during a scare.

faq.question: Is cash runway the same as profit?
faq.answer: No. Profit is an accounting result; runway is about cash timing. Profitable businesses run out of cash regularly.

faq.question: What is a healthy cash runway?
faq.answer: There is no universal number, but under three months leaves no room to absorb a late payment or a slow season.

formula.expression: Cash runway (months) = Cash on hand ÷ Average monthly net cash outflow
formula.note: Use a three-month average outflow so one unusual month does not flatter or wreck the figure.
